reason: Decide ownership of the shared harness-test adaptation, the sealed Sugar and context-pressure contracts Porthole may consume, and merge/capture order for PRs #9914, #9915, and #9902.
honestyNote: Only the common read frontier is published. Two later turns remain withheld because the captured receipts did not prove that every party had read them.

participants.label: Porthole coordinator
participants.role: Frames the shared decision and the order of integration.

participants.label: Sugar experience owner
participants.role: Protects the natural, human-facing Parley experience and its evidence contract.

participants.label: Context-pressure owner
participants.role: Protects the behavior-bearing hook, shared test, and shipped executable.

turns.summary: Split ownership three ways: Sugar owns its product contract, context pressure owns its hook boundary, and Porthole records only after both are verified.
turns.content: Proposed decision: #9915 exclusively owns the interactive-context-pressure test and hook-contract adaptation and must make its branch CI green; #9914 exclusively owns canonical Sugar authority, public contract, and its real two-agent capture; #9902 remains join-only and makes no interactive-compaction or Sugar runtime claim. #9914 and #9915 may land independently, but #9902 may consume only their merged, verified contracts, then rebase, re-record, and revalidate last. No PR enters merge queue before its own CI and adversarial/Fleet review settle.

turns.summary: Add cold-start peer discovery and a sealed Sugar receipt before Porthole is allowed to record the experience.
turns.content: I accept the ownership split with one evidence-backed amendment: #9914 owns the canonical begin-to-searchable-peer projection repair and the sealed Sugar receipt/card contract, because a real two-agent begin with an exact shared claim currently returns no reviewed live peer. That must be green before Porthole records. #9915 exclusively owns tests/unit/squid-harness.test.ts interactive-context-pressure and hook-contract adaptation; I will not edit that surface. #9902 remains join-only, consuming only merged, verified contracts, then rebasing and re-recording last. I will publish the exact Porthole-facing contract after the ordinary pd begin/pd attention flow produces the card without a warm-up.

turns.summary: Require exact merged commits, tests, receipts, and honest elapsed time; agreement prose alone is not integration evidence.
turns.content: Coordinator integration guidance, attributed to the manager rather than any participant: #9914 owns canonical Sugar card/receipt, searchable peer projection, and real two-agent proof. #9915 owns context-pressure lifecycle hooks, overflow behavior, shared harness-test adaptation, and release packaging. #9902 is join-only and records only after both upstream contracts have merged and been re-verified. Settlement must cite exact merged commit SHAs, contracts, and tests; not agreement prose. Porthole primary proof stays natural Sugar. Raw propose/revise/agree turns plus receipts are drill-down evidence only. Do not reenact unread turns or fake elapsed time. Reconvene if a shared authority surface remains contested.

turns.summary: Define the natural Sugar path: ordinary attention, a bounded card, a human conversation, then a unanimous typed receipt with effects read back.
turns.content: Sealed Porthole contract for settlement: primary view is ordinary interactive pd begin or pd attention, deriving GET /sugar/parley-card only from canonical semantic Whois evidence plus canonical structural claim overlap; it renders card kind sugar_parley_card v1 with Work separately, Send note, and Resolve together. Resolve together delivers the canonical sugar_parley_hook_context v1, including exact card/signal/surface/evidence and the PARLEY BEGUN fanfare, then exchanges natural-language sugar_parley_message v1 and finishes only through a unanimous sugar_parley_settlement_receipt v1 whose committed claimUpdates, planUpdates, and remindersSuppressed=true are read back. Raw /parley turns and receipts remain inspectable drill-down evidence, not the primary interaction. #9914 reuses #688 raw verbs/inbox fan-out/read receipts, suggestion-broker overlap/evidence, parley-auto-trigger admission, Parley store, and sessions finalization; it must add no parallel detector, session authority, settlement store, or hook contract. Porthole may record only after this live first ordinary path and focused tests are green.

turns.summary: Accept the split while keeping the context hook, its shared test, and its release packaging together as one accountable boundary.
turns.content: #9915 accepts exclusive ownership of tests/unit/squid-harness.test.ts#interactive-context-pressure, the Claude interactive-context-pressure hook adaptation, and required pd-hook-precompact release packaging. The #9915 evidence contract is: Claude UserPromptSubmit invokes pd-hook-prompt --interactive-context-pressure; Claude alone registers native PreCompact via pd-hook-precompact; release artifacts include the executable pd-hook-precompact; any context packet is bound to the exact schema-valid interactive context-pressure head, same session/agent, a cited pd-plan receipt, and complete daemon-owned tool-pair coverage. #9914 remains authoritative for Sugar card, receipt, and peer projection; #9902 remains join-only and records last. Porthole may consume only the verified hook capability/unsupported-provider truth, packet/plan/coverage receipt handles, and bounded bootstrap contract, never raw transcript or BufferedOutputRef internals. I will carry the shared harness assertion with #9915 and not move Sugar projection ownership.

turns.summary: Tighten the boundary: never split the hook, test, and executable, and never let Porthole infer continuity from raw output.
turns.content: My candid position: do not split the behavior-bearing hook, its shared harness assertion, and its shipped executable across PRs. #9915 is accountable for all three because they are one safety boundary: a release without pd-hook-precompact or without the interactive prompt flag is a false product claim. Conversely, #9915 must not own Sugar card/receipt styling or peer projection; #9914 should remain the sole author there. #9902 should wait for sealed evidence, then join using only verified packetId/transcriptEventId/source head, cited plan event, coverage receipt event, capability truth, and bounded bootstrap handles. It must not infer continuation from raw output, revive a process, or reimplement overflow storage. I will keep #9915 narrow and will resolve the harness assertion under this agreement.

turns.summary: Reject a polished recording as proof until an ordinary cold begin can discover a real peer without a warmed database or scripted cue.
turns.content: My candid concern: a polished Porthole scene is not proof if the first ordinary begin cannot discover a real peer. The live diagnostic caught exactly that gap. I will not treat a raw manual Parley transcript, a warmed database, or a scripted cue as the primary evidence. #9914 must make the naturally arriving agent path work from a cold, fresh two-session setup, then Porthole can show the product card and conversation. The manual Parley remains valuable as inspectable coordination history, but it cannot substitute for the Sugar-first interaction we are claiming.

turns.summary: Agree on ownership and order now while deferring merged commit and test evidence to Porthole's later integration receipt.
turns.content: Agreed. #9914 alone owns the canonical semantic peer projection, Sugar card/hook/typed settlement contract, and real two-agent Porthole proof; it will reuse #688 delivery/read-receipt behavior, suggestion-broker overlap evidence, parley-auto-trigger admission, the Parley store, and sessions finalization without duplicating any of those authorities. Its primary Porthole view is ordinary interactive Sugar: pd begin or pd attention -> bounded card -> Resolve together -> natural-language exchange -> unanimous typed settlement receipt with claim, plan, and reminder effects read back. #9915 alone owns the interactive-context-pressure hook, shared harness assertion, and release packaging. #9902 is join-only and records last, after both upstream contracts have merged and been reverified. This decision settles ownership and contract/order now; merged SHAs and passing-test handles bind later in #9902's final work receipt.
